# Vendored public-domain source texts

Full text of editions this build's quote records cite, committed so that
wording can be verified *reproducibly* -- by any session, at any time,
without network access. That matters here for a specific reason: the
sandbox this project's agents run in blocks every patristic text host
(ccel.org, newadvent.org, wikisource, archive.org, gutenberg, tertullian.org),
so before these files existed a quote record could not be verified at all
and `gate_quote_fidelity_recording` had nothing honest to record.

**This file is GENERATED, not hand-edited** -- run
`python cic/engine/texts_registry.py --write-readme` after vendoring a new
file or adding an entry to cic/texts/REGISTRY.yaml. Editing this table directly
will be overwritten the next time it runs. See `cic/texts/INTAKE.md` for the
full procedure, from an attached file to a vendored, registered, findable text.

PUBLIC DOMAIN ONLY. Every file here must be out of copyright, and its own
provenance header must say so -- the `rights` column below is read fresh
from each file's own header every time this report runs, not trusted from
a claim made when the file was added. In-copyright editions (Holmes 2007,
Ward 1975) are referenced by `source` record and never vendored --
committing them would be redistribution.

`lang` is blank for English (the default when a file has no `Language:` line)
and an ISO 639-3 code otherwise -- an original-language witness, not a
translation; see `cic/texts/INTAKE.md`.

Volumen primum: Acta patriarchatus Constantinopolitani MCCCXV-MCCCCII, e codicibus manu scriptis bibliothecae Palatinae Vindobonensis, tomus prior. Franz Miklosich and Joseph Muller (eds.); the register of the Patriarchate of Constantinople, 1315 to 1402, Greek with Latin summaries and notes. Vienna: Carolus Gerold, 1860 ('VINDOBONAE CAROLUS GEROLD MDCCCLX'). Language: Greek with Latin. RIGHTS: public domain by date. Evidence: the title page reads 'MDCCCLX' (1860) in this scan's OCR (file lines 143 and 182); host record: date 1860, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Fetched directly (curl, raw bytes) from the Internet Archive item actaetdiplomata00graegoog, the item's own _djvu.txt; header prepended, body unaltered (long s glyph occurs 2 times and was left as found; nothing stripped, corrected, re-spaced or retyped). Witness grade: primary text; Greek polytonic good with breathing slips; Latin headings clean. Size: 2.47 MB. The first volume of Miklosich and Muller, the patriarchal register edited from the Vienna manuscripts: decisions, letters, synodal acts and appeals of the Patriarchate of Constantinople from 1315 to 1402, printed in Greek with a Latin heading for each document; the contents list at the end runs to documents of 1372-1374 on page 594-595. The file ends with that contents list. The volume includes the documents on the Palamite and Akindynist quarrel and on parish and monastic discipline. The second half of the register (1364-1402, 'tomus alter', volume 2 of 1862) was not found on the host. A second scan, actaetdiplomata01miklgoog (1.5 MB), is a photomechanical reprint with much poorer OCR and was not vendored.

Structurally better for this build's own purposes: shorter/longer/Syriac recensions are addressable by id (e.g. v.v.iv-p1 vs v.v.iv-p4 for Romans 4), and footnotes are their own <note> elements rather than interleaved apparatus text - both real friction points hand-transcribing the plain text had already hit. Extracting text correctly requires walking element trees properly, not naive regex: a lazy `<p>...</p>` match truncates early against nested <note><p class="endnote">...</p></note> structures, and a node's own skip-tag status must not be applied to its `tail` text - both mistakes were made and caught live during this swap, on the Smyrnaeans and Martyrdom-of-Polycarp passages respectively, before anything was recommitted.

- **`aphrahat_demonstrations-2-7_hallock1932.txt`** -- Aphrahat the Persian Sage, Demonstration VII (On Penitents) and Demonstration II (On Love), trans. Frank H. Acquired to close the split named on srcSYR010's scope determination: NPNF2-13 carries eight of the 23 Demonstrations, and syrlex007 cites 'Dem. 6:8 and 7:20' in one breath, 6 being in that eight and 7 not. Demonstration II is a bonus - no record cites it yet. RTF attachment converted mechanically by the same purpose-written reader used for the Ephraim file; no content passed through model-generated output.

RIGHTS - THE FIRST FILE IN THIS CORPUS THAT DOES NOT CLEAR THE DATE RULE, so the basis is recorded here rather than assumed. Every other file here is public domain by publication date alone (ANF/NPNF, Mitchell 1912/1921, Clarke 1918, Phillips 1876), which is the 'to ~1929' line the Presence Gate Spec's own path table states. Hallock's translation is 1932: in the US, works published 1930-1963 are public domain only where copyright was not renewed, and no renewal check has been performed. What this file rests on instead is the transcriber's own explicit declaration, present verbatim in the file - Roger Pearse, Ipswich, 2006, declaring all material on the page public domain - the same declaration the Palladius and Doctrine of Addai files already rest on, and there confirmed by grep on the page itself.

The gap was flagged before vendoring and the file was HELD rather than vendored while it was open. Mark ruled on 2026-08-18, in these words: 'vendor it, pearse's declaration is enough.' Recorded as a project-lead act, with the reasoning visible, so that a later reader can see this file's basis differs in kind from its neighbours' and can revisit it without having to rediscover why.

'uerba epistulae'"), making it a further significant repository of preserved Donatist voice alongside the Petilian material already relied on at rows 4/12. LIII' by name (CSEL's own numbers for Pars I, II and III): the file is a binding of Pars I, Pars II and Pars III in that order. CONTENT CONFIRMED THIS SESSION: Boyd's essay (roughly the first 45% of the file, title page at 'WILLIAM K. BOYD, Ph.D.') gives an extensive narrative history of Donatist-targeted legislation in C. Th. Book 16 Title 5, naming the Circumcellions directly and quoting several individual laws verbatim in Latin (e.g. xvi.5.28, xvi.5.41, both naming the Donatists by name), citing the chain xvi.5.3 through xvi.5.58 including the 405 edict (xvi.5.38-39) that Doc_02's own 'Edict of Unity' material rests on. NOTE: xvi.5.52 specifically (the source_registry row-16 circumcelliones/agonistici citation) is not quoted verbatim anywhere in this file - Boyd's own citation chain runs '...51, 54, 55...' past it without quoting it directly; this file corroborates the surrounding legislative sequence and the Donatist material generally but does not itself supply that one specific law's own wording. The term 'agonistici' (the group's own self-designation) does not appear anywhere in this file; Boyd uses only 'Circumcellions' throughout, consistent with early-20th-century scholarly usage. OCR QUALITY: generally cleaner than the raw 19th-century critical-edition scans elsewhere in this corpus, but still carries scattered letter-substitution errors; any specific quotation drawn from it needs visual cross-check against its own surrounding context before being relied on for a verbatim claim.

Pars III (Cyprian's Opera Spuria, the Vita Caecilii Cypriani, the Acta Proconsularia, and the volume's own indices and praefatio) is now also vendored, as that world's Registry row 194 (2026-09-08), closing G1 in full -- corrected here 2026-09-08, from an earlier draft's own present-tense "is not included and remains unacquired; G1 stays open for that part only," stale since that acquisition and left uncorrected through twenty-two rounds of that world's own independent review, since no sweep of that review had been scoped to this file. Public domain by date (1868/1871, both far past the ~95-year US threshold); the 1965 Johnson Reprint Corporation printing this scan derives from is a photomechanical reprint of the same public-domain text, no new claim over it. Mechanically extracted from a docx Mark compiled from an archive.org "Full text" view of a Google Books scan. The exact item identifier, not stated when supplied, is now independently confirmed rather than guessed -- confirmed here, independent review Round 24's own M3: sthascicaecilic01hartgoog, matched character for character against the vendored file at both ends -- see the file's own header. Site-navigation chrome and Google's own standard PD usage notice stripped, doubled inter-word spacing normalized, nothing else altered. OCR quality is uneven: the running Latin text reads cleanly throughout (including right at the end, where Epistle 81 closes with no truncation), but the apparatus criticus carries real, localized OCR noise -- garbled manuscript sigla, stray characters -- disclosed in the file's own header rather than treated as pristine. Original-language witness (Latin) -- second-witness caveat applies per cic/texts/INTAKE.md: never primary evidence for a Representative on its own.

CONVERTER NOTE: striprtf (used for Palladius) is not installed here and LibreOffice would not load the file, so the conversion used a purpose-written RTF reader. Its first output shattered words across lines ('Teache/r/s', 'long p/eriod') because it emitted the source file's own line-wrapping; in RTF a bare CR/LF is insignificant whitespace and only \par marks a break. Fixed and re-run, then verified by locating a broken token intact. That mattered here more than usual: a vendored text exists to have quotations LOCATED in it, and one with words split mid-token would have failed silently at exactly that job. Structural integrity confirmed: both volumes present in the one file, with the five Discourses to Hypatius and Vol. II's 'Of Domnus', Against Marcion I-III, Against Bardaisan, On Virginity and Against Mani all located by their own section headings. A bibliographic header (title/creator/rights, matching the Palladius convention) was prepended - the RTF carried none. This is the acquisition that reverses srcSYR007's paraphrase-only determination of 2026-08-18, by the route that determination itself named.

Surfaced by the same 2026-09-13 source-research routine while chasing a manuscript-catalogued "epistula Eucherii ad Salonium" (a short prefatory letter listed in this edition's own manuscript-contents apparatus, p. VIII-VIIII); this build thread's own direct read of the file confirms that specific short letter is NOT separately printed or edited anywhere in this volume, only catalogued as existing in one manuscript - what IS genuinely present and newly vendored are the two full works above (Formulae addressed to Veranus, Instructiones addressed to Salonius). Latin only; no public-domain English translation of either work was found. **A significant find beyond what was searched for:** Instructionum liber I's own praefatio ad Salonium directly names Honoratus as "primo insularum postea etiam ecclesiarum magistro," Hilary of Arles as the island's own teacher ("beatissimi Hilarii tunc insulani tironis sed iam nunc summi pontificis"), and Salvian and Vincent of Lerins together as those who "consummantibus... eloquentia pariter scientiaque praeeminentibus" completed Salonius's formation - the Latin original, independently vendored for the first time, of the Salvian/Vincent co-teacher testimony gallic_Source_Registry.md row 43 already flags as "quoted in translation by Sanford but not yet independently vendored in Latin." The same volume's own appendix also carries a real letter from Salvian to Eucherius ("Domino et dulci suo Eucherio episcopo Saluianus"), praising the Instructiones on receipt - a direct primary attestation of the Salvian-Eucherius relationship, not previously in this world's vendored library. This material is squarely Native (the Lerins teaching-circle's own composition), not merely tangential exegesis. Formulae's own content (an allegorical-interpretation glossary addressed to Veranus) remains the more tangential of the two works, genre-wise. Corpus-map assigned same day (Native, tradition role) - see gallic_Source_Registry.md row 46. NOT the Ewald-Hartmann edition itself (that remains unvendored) - but its own front matter states directly that its text and notes are taken FROM the Ewald-Hartmann edition, and every included letter carries an explicit editorial concordance to that edition's own book/ epistle numbering. Fetched as a PDF directly from Google's own download endpoint (volume ID KCRJAQAAMAAJ, confirmed via Google Books API metadata as public-domain/open-access/full-view), converted to plain text via pdftotext -layout (reading the PDF's own embedded OCR text layer, no re-OCR, no model-generated content). RIGHTS: 1907 publication date alone. CONTENT CONFIRMED THIS SESSION: searched the whole file directly (not page-by-page) for 'Donatist' and its Latin case forms. Four genuine Donatist-subject letters found, each independently verified in context and each carrying the edition's own explicit Ewald/Hartmann concordance: this edition's Ep. LXXXII = Ewald lib. II, ep. 46 (to Columbus of Numidia, re: Maximianus of Pudentiana corrupted by the Donatists, 592 Jul); Ep. LXXXIV = Ewald lib. IV, ep. 32 (to Pantaleon, praetorian prefect of Africa, urging suppression of the Donatists, 594 Jul); Ep. LXXXVI = Ewald lib. IV, ep. 35 (to Victor and Columbus, bishops of Africa, urging a council against the Donatists, 594 Jul); Ep. LXXXVII = Hartmann lib. V, ep. 3 (to Dominicus of Carthage, on heretic-coercion and a 594 council at Carthage against the Donatists per a quoted Dudden 1905 footnote, 594 Sept). These are IN ADDITION TO letters I.72 and I.75, already confirmed genuine elsewhere in this world's own build record by a prior session's independent check; this file's own selection does not draw from Book I at all, so it neither confirms nor contradicts those two. No letter numbered I.73 was found in this selection. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is a SELECTION ('Epistolae Selectae'), not the complete Register - its own title page states 'Pars I' and its own back matter confirms a Pars II exists, not located or vendored this session. Fetched directly from archive.org by the Library thread, October 2026; header prepended, no text altered. Höfler's second volume, 24 numbered items, among them the 'Chronicon Taboritarum' of John of Lukavec and Nicholas of Pelhřimov (called Biskupec), the Taborite priests' account of their case against the Prague masters, with the priests' 'Responsio ... ad scriptum magistrorum' (item XXIV). The Chronicon prints the Taborite priests' five articles (printed pp. 478-479, said to have been preached to the mountain gathering of 1419: priests holding no land or rents by civil title, tithes as freely given support and not a debt, priests giving up civil lordship, the Gospel law as sufficient for the church without the old-law ceremonies and added rites, and flight from thieves and robbers who climb in by another way), a footnote at the foot of p. 700 marks the end of the 'confessio Thaboritarum' (the Chronicon's first part) and cites p. 503 of a Rotterdam printing of 1616, and Part II (printed p. 701 ff.) tells the Bohemians' hearing at the Council of Basel on the four articles of Prague; the 'Tractatus de origine Hussitarum' (item XIX), a Catholic polemic that names the Adamites and the Taborites; Hus's letters and the Prague university papers. The strongest inside Taborite text found, and the nearest the shelf has to the Taborite articles and the Four Articles of Prague as the Hussites argued them; the Chronicon is a Taborite document, the Tractatus a hostile one. No public-domain English translation is vendored. WITNESS: Primary Latin sources including the Taborite priests' chronicle, readable with scattered errors; quote after checking the scan.

MARTYREM LUCIANUM" confirmed present (identifier patrologicursusc0050unse), with the editorial Monitum naming Lucian's death by starvation under Maximinus, matching the story's own framing. IMPORTANT: a first, more standard-looking identifier for this same volume (patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_050) was also fetched and found completely unusable - its OCR applied a Greek-only character recognizer to the whole bilingual page, garbling both the Greek and the Latin translation into unreadable pseudo-Greek text (0% Latin-alphabet-legible by direct measurement) - do not use that identifier for this volume. This file's own identifier is materially better but is not itself fully clean: zero Greek-script characters are recoverable from it either, so Chrysostom's own Greek is not present here - only Fronton du Duc's Latin translation is genuinely readable. Serves antiochene-church-third-century.

Reading its own division titles, the NPNF selection is De Synodis, De Trinitate, three Homilies on Psalms, and John of Damascus's Exposition of the Orthodox Faith; Hilary's historical/polemical works are not translated here. WHAT IT DOES CARRY, which is worth more than what was asked for: Hilary's De Synodis reproduces the Eastern creeds verbatim with their numbered anathemas ('If any man says that the Father and the Son are two Gods: let him be anathema') across a 167,000-character span, plus the Homoean formula that the Son is 'like the Father in all things, as Scripture says.' That resolves the caveat on the imperial scrub's finding 4: those creeds were previously reachable only through npnf204 (Athanasius's De Synodis), and srcIJC24 excludes the Athanasius corpus beyond the single Julius quotation. Hilary is an independent Latin transmitter of the same texts, so the exclusion does not apply and no owner decision is needed to use them. Vendored for future reference; no quote or source record cites it yet.

- **`webbe_world-english-bible-british-edition.xml`** -- THE FIRST BIBLE IN THIS CORPUS, and it is here for one narrow job: the SPOKEN layer of a quote record whose figure is quoting scripture. Mark's two-layer wording ruling (2026-08-19) gives each quote a historical wording and a plain modern one; where the father is quoting scripture, the modern layer may not carry this build's own paraphrase of a verse, so it needs a modern translation that is genuinely free. Three records were held pending this file: halq003 (Matt 6:21), ijcq010 (Ps 116:15), pahcq005 (Deut 6:5, Lev 19:18, Matt 22:37/39). NOTE WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the Bible remains outside the six worlds' EVIDENCE base by design - these worlds are post-apostolic and are reconstructed from what they themselves wrote. This file is a wording source for verses a father already quotes, never a source of evidence about a world. WHICH EDITION AND WHY. The British Edition (WEBBE), not the main WEB, because the main edition renders the divine name 'Yahweh' and the British and Messianic editions render it 'LORD' - Mark chose LORD, and Ps 116:15 is one of the three held verses, so the difference was live rather than theoretical. The cost is British spelling ('neighbour' in Lev 19:18 and Matt 22:39), which is the trade the only LORD-rendering non-Messianic edition carries. PROVENANCE. ebible.org is blocked by this sandbox's egress policy - the same condition this module's own WHY records for every patristic host, and the reason the corpus is vendored at all - so the file came through the seven1m/open-bibles mirror of eBible.org's USFX distribution. It authenticates itself rather than resting on the mirror: it names itself the World English Bible British Edition, references eBible.org's usfx.xsd schema, and carries the WEB preface's own public-domain declaration, which is what rights_declared() reads. A bibliographic header was prepended for the same reason as Palladius and the Doctrine of Addai - the distribution carries no 'Rights:' line of its own and its prose declaration sits far past the 100-line read window - but written as an XML COMMENT rather than plain text, so the file stays valid XML for ElementTree.
